name: Second-wave feminism
summary: Second-wave feminism, the women's movement of the 1960s and 1970s, held that women's inequality ran beyond the vote into work, law, family and sexuality. Its liberal wing around NOW demanded the Equal Rights Amendment, enforcement of the ban on sex discrimination, child care, maternity leave and the repeal of abortion laws, and called for marriage to become an equal partnership. Its radical wing around the Redstockings, Millett and Firestone analysed male supremacy as the oldest and deepest form of domination, held that gender is imposed by social conditioning, and called for a revolution going beyond reform.
scope: The American women's liberation movement of about 1963 to 1980 as Britannica defines it, in two wings: the liberal wing, represented by NOW's 1966 Statement of Purpose and 1967 Bill of Rights, and the radical wing, represented by the Redstockings manifesto, Millett's 1968 lecture on sexual politics, Firestone's Dialectic of Sex (chapter 1) and 'On Abortion', and Koedt's 1968 speech (read, not cited). Positions are recorded only where these texts state them; where only one wing speaks the answer rests on that wing's text, and where the wings differ it is a split. Excludes first-wave suffrage feminism and later third-wave, intersectional, queer or anti-pornography feminisms.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Firestone states that 'the division of labour would be ended' as the first sexual division of labour is abolished, as part of the end of the biological family and of class systems.

abortion-legal.rationale: NOW's 1967 Bill of Rights demands removing the laws governing abortion from the penal codes, and Firestone's 1968 speech 'On Abortion' calls for free abortion and says 'those bodies belong to us'.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Firestone writes that 'the division of labour would be ended by the elimination of labour altogether (through cybernetics)', which means using automation to cut necessary work.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Millett rejects 'the white man's imperialist racism' and the burning of villages in Vietnam, and compares male dominance to racial domination, so rule of one group over another for its own good is not endorsed.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Firestone rejects laws made by a male lawmaking body that excludes women, and Millett says the ballot 'means nothing at all if you are not represented in a representative democracy'.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Bill of Rights puts first the Equal Rights Amendment: 'Equality of rights under the law shall not be denied or abridged ... on account of sex', which rules out law that assigns different public roles to each sex.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: NOW's first demand is a constitutional amendment, immediately ratified by the states, guaranteeing equality of rights under the law regardless of sex.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: NOW's Statement of Purpose says 'human rights for all are indivisible' and pledges support for 'the common cause of equal rights for all those who suffer discrimination and deprivation'.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Bill of Rights demands that the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission enforce the ban on sex discrimination in employment 'with the same vigor' as the ban on racial discrimination, which leaves employers no freedom to choose whom to hire by sex.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The Statement of Purpose complains that the commissions on the status of women 'have power only to advise' and no power to enforce, and the Bill of Rights demands that the EEOC enforce the ban on sex discrimination.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Millett states that 'the whole structure of male and female personality is arbitrarily imposed by social conditioning', with traits such as aggression and tenderness assigned to one sex or the other.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: NOW says women's problems 'are linked to many broader questions of social justice' requiring 'concerted action by many groups', and Millett argues racial and economic crimes cannot be solved unless the oppression of all people ends, a revolution in sexual politics being basic to it.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Firestone argues that Engels's economic account of history 'does not go deep enough' and rewrites it to seek the ultimate cause of historical events in 'the dialectic of sex'.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Bill of Rights asks the state for paid maternity leave, child care facilities 'established by law on the same basis as parks, libraries and public schools', and revised welfare law, well beyond protecting people from physical violence.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Firestone says that 'unless we have a part in creating the laws which govern our fate, then we will refuse to follow those dictates and laws', so legal status alone does not bind women excluded from lawmaking.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Millett calls the relation of the sexes one of dominance and subordination throughout history, with every avenue of power in male hands, and the Redstockings manifesto says men 'have controlled all political, economic and cultural institutions'.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Statement of Purpose says 'true equality of opportunity and freedom of choice for women requires' practical measures such as a nationwide network of child-care centres, so it ties freedom of choice to material means.

racial-franchise.rationale: NOW demands 'equality of civil and political rights' for women 'as well as for Negroes and other deprived groups', which leaves no room for limiting the vote to one ethnic group.

racial-oppression-before-sexism.rationale: The Redstockings manifesto calls male supremacy 'the oldest, most basic form of domination' and racism and capitalism 'extensions of male supremacy', so it does not put racial oppression first.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Statement of Purpose asks that the Constitution's protection of civil rights be applied for women 'as well as for Negroes and other deprived groups', and pledges support for equal rights for all who suffer discrimination, so law enforcing racial segregation is opposed.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Millett writes that religion 'takes the enforcement of male supremacy by divine fiat as part of its function in a patriarchy' and traces the subordination of women through Jewish and Christian teaching.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Statement of Purpose aims to 'advance the unfinished revolution of women toward true equality, now', and Firestone calls for a feminist revolution, so neither seeks to restore an earlier order.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Firestone holds that sex class 'sprang directly from a biological reality: men and women were created different', while arguing that the resulting social system can be ended.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Statement of Purpose rejects the idea that home and family are 'primarily woman's world ... hers, to dominate' and demands 'a true partnership between the sexes' with 'an equitable sharing of the responsibilities of home and children'.

state-harmful.rationale: NOW calls on government to enforce anti-discrimination law and to pass the Equal Rights Amendment, and the Bill of Rights asks for child care established by law, which cannot be squared with abolishing the state.

traditional-family.rationale: NOW calls for 'a different concept of marriage' than the present division of roles, and Firestone argues that the family must be uprooted for exploitation to end, though NOW itself keeps marriage and family as institutions.

unpaid-domestic-work-exploitation.rationale: The Redstockings manifesto says women 'are exploited as sex objects, breeders, domestic servants, and cheap labor'.

war-builds-character.rationale: Millett rejects the 'military male ideal' and 'the habits of violence, warfare' and calls the self-definition of virility through oppression something that 'has got to go'.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Statement of Purpose names 'the churches' and 'religion' among the fields where it will 'break through the silken curtain of prejudice and discrimination against women'.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Equal Rights Amendment NOW demands would bar any law that imposes a duty on one sex only, so a law requiring women alone to cover themselves cannot stand beside it.

women-organise-apart-from-men.rationale: NOW's founders are 'men and women' organising together in partnership, while the Redstockings manifesto is a women's organisation building unity among women and asks men only to give up privilege and support them, so the movement's own texts point both ways.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Equal Rights Amendment demanded first in the Bill of Rights says equality of rights under the law may not be denied on account of sex, so women's legal rights to land cannot differ from men's.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Statement of Purpose calls for 'equality of civil and political rights and responsibilities on behalf of women' and for women to take full part in party committees, candidate selection and running for office.

missingStatements.text: Women should have the legal right to control their own reproduction, including access to contraception.
missingStatements.rationale: NOW's Bill of Rights demanded the right to control reproductive lives and the pill and Title X were milestones; broader than the abortion statement.

missingStatements.text: Employers should be legally prohibited from discriminating on the basis of sex in hiring, pay and promotion.
missingStatements.rationale: Equal Pay Act, Title VII and NOW's enforcement campaigns were core demands.

missingStatements.text: Rape and domestic violence within marriage should be treated as crimes like any other.
missingStatements.rationale: The movement exposed marital rape and domestic violence and built rape crisis centres and shelters.
missingStatements.declined: Near-universal consensus today, so test takers would not split on it (fails the contested bar).

missingStatements.text: Child care should be provided publicly for all families who want it.
missingStatements.rationale: NOW's founding statement and its Bill of Rights both call for a nationwide public network of child care.

notes: Rules 7 pass of 2026-11-14. The earlier answers rested on Wikipedia summaries; they were re-checked against the movement's own texts and defining reference works, and kept only where a text states a position that settles the statement (the earlier answers stay in each reviewHistory). Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means, globalism. The texts say little on ecology, globalism, most of government and most of the economy, so those statements are null. Anti-pornography and sex-work debates are described only in general feminist scholarship (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy), not in these texts, so they stay null. The Spirit of Houston report (1977) is listed in notFound.
